South Carolina Senator Darlene Graham says it's up to President Trump
to decide whether he'll enforce new sanctions against Russia.
Those sanctions were in a bill sponsored by her late brother, Senator Lindsey Graham.
Trump announced a waiver for the sanctions just days before they were take effect.
It's up to him whether or not he chooses to use it.
Personally, I would choose to keep the pressure on Russia
to end the war and get the gas prices down.
Trump's decision has since brought bipartisan condemnation from Capitol Hill.
President Trump says he is changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico

Republicans have been facing strong political headwinds

Lawyers for Congresswoman Ilan Omar are demanding that the Justice Department
return all property seized by federal agents in a search over Minnesota home this week
and, as NPR's Ryan Lucas reports,
they also say the investigation targeting Omar is a political one.
In a letter to the Justice Department, Omar's attorneys call the investigation
a vindictive, retributive, and politically motivated effort
to go after one of President Trump's chief critics in Congress.
They point out that the court-authorized search of Omar's home in Washington, D.C.
took place just weeks before the midterm elections,
which violates a long-standing Justice Department norm
that aims to avoid taking action that could be perceived as interfering in an election.
Federal agents seized Omar's phone, computer, and documents
during their search of her home as part of an investigation
into possible immigration fraud.
Omar was born in Somalia and came to the U.S. as a child.
Her attorneys say there is no legitimate basis to suggest
that Omar violated any law concerning her citizenship status.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News.
A fire at a Canadian military base in the province of Alberta
has resulted in several deaths and injuries.
As Dan Karpenschuck reports,
Canada's Defence Minister would not confirm the number of casualties,
saying it is still an active and delicate situation.
Defence Minister David McGinty says he saddened to share the news
there have been fatalities and injuries as a result
of an incident at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright,
outside the community of Wainwright, about 120 miles east of Edmonton.
He says a large, fast-moving fire pushed by strong winds
spread into the region, with first responders working to protect people,
property, and critical infrastructure.
Air ambulances have been dispatched from Edmonton and Saskatoon.
The Royal Canadian Mounted Police is investigating early reports
of a fire at the base's training area.
It's where training is conducted in realistic battlefield conditions.
Prime Minister Mark Carney, who is in Alberta, offered condolences,
saying his thoughts are with the brave women and men affected.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karpenschuck in Toronto.
And this is NPR News.
The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-64 Saturday
in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals.
From member station KALW, Jordan Carnes has our reports.
Saturday's game marked the Valkyries' first appearance in the Finals,
while the Dream's last visit was in 2013.
Both teams surprised the league with dominant playoff runs,
each sweeping the former consecutive champs, the Aces,
and the Liberty in the semifinals.
Game 1 was marked by defense.
The Valkyries are the top-ranked defensive team in the league,
while the Dream's Angel Reiss was named Defensive Player of the Year.
However, it wasn't enough to beat the Valkyries on their home turf,
Ballhalla, which has sold out every game in its two years.
Game 2 of the Best of Seven series will be on Monday in San Francisco.
For NPR News, I'm Jordan Carnes.
Israel's military is condemning a Saturday attack by settlers
in the occupied West Bank on a group of European diplomats
calling it severe active violence.
The diplomats say the settlers were using metal bars in the attack
and were targeting people from Belgium, France, and Poland.
At least four people have been killed since the olive harvest began
in the Palestinian territory earlier this month.
In Kenya, three health workers are now testing positive for Ebola.
They had been caring for the country's first confirmed case,
a man who had returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo
where an Ebola outbreak continues.
The number of confirmed cases has now risen to seven in Kenya.
The first person diagnosed died on October 5th.
At least 4,300 people have died in Congo since the outbreak there began.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
